mechanism: Proving non-membership in a committed state set. An {{agent}} cryptographically commits to its full state (e.g., via Merkle tree), then uses a Zero-Knowledge Range Proof to demonstrate that a specific {{value}} or datum is NOT present in that committed set, without revealing what the set contains. Operates via exhaustive search over the committed domain, treating verified failure-to-find as proof of absence within that snapshot. The guarantee is bounded: it proves non-membership in the committed tree, not global non-possession—the agent could hold uncommitted state elsewhere.
gloss: Proving non-membership in a committed state snapshot
failure_modes: Incomplete commitment: state is held outside the committed tree, so the proof is valid and practically meaningless.
Stale commitment: the state changed between commitment and verification.
Cost: proving absence over a large domain is expensive, and the expense scales with the domain rather than with the {{value}} being checked.
invariants: Proves non-membership in the committed set only, never global non-possession.
The search covers the whole committed domain.
Names the commitment it proves against, and when that commitment was made.
preconditions: Closed world assumption (over the committed state, not globally)
State commitment is fresh and complete
postconditions: H proved false within committed state
